mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases consistently over 6 months and the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of the periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and can cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 5% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 70% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the S&P 500 still produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1), it signals strong consumer demand outpacing economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth > GDPC1 YoY growth
failure_condition: If RSAFS YoY growth exceeds GDPC1 YoY growth and the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day forward returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM increase > 0.1% and UNRATE MoM decrease > 0.1%
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.1% month-over-month and the S&P 500 still produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month and the S&P 500 still produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 70% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during a late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 YoY growth is less than 1% and the S&P 500 still produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances during a late-cycle expansion.
